methodology: Attempted the 2025 Pornhub Insights Year in Review first, per instructions, since it would have published around Dec 2025/Jan 2026. Direct requests to pornhub.com/insights (via ExaContents and via curl) returned HTTP 403 in this environment. Located an archived copy of the official page via the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=pornhub.com/insights/2025-year-in-review), which resolved to a snapshot captured 2026-06-24. Fetched that snapshot directly with curl (HTTP 200, ~189KB HTML) and parsed it with BeautifulSoup to extract clean article text (~66KB). This text contains: (1) a narrative paragraph naming a subset of state-level top relative searches, and (2) a full 'Top 20 Countries in Detail' section with a dedicated subsection per country covering top search terms, top pornstars, trending searches, top categories, and (for most countries) top relative categories. Because the narrative text alone named only ~19 states, the page's embedded infographic images were also located (65 tags found) and the specific PNG titled '...year-in-review-map-united-states.png' (the 'United States Top Relative Searches' choropleth map) was downloaded directly from the Wayback Machine's image mirror. This image was read at full resolution and at 2x-3x zoomed crops (Pacific/West region, Midwest region, Northeast/New England region) to transcribe every state label and its paired search term, including verifying the connector lines for the dense New England cluster (Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut) by tracing each line's color against its text color. This image is the authoritative, complete source for the state layer -- it is Pornhub's own primary infographic, not a press paraphrase. Two independent press articles (Advocate.com and DNYUZ/New York Post syndication) were used to cross-check a total of 8 of the 29 transcribed state entries against the primary image reading; both matched with zero discrepancies (see cross_check_results below). For the country layer, no separate image extraction was needed because the 'Top 20 Countries in Detail' prose text was complete and unambiguous for all 20 countries listed in the page's own table of contents (United States, Mexico, Philippines, Brazil, Germany, France, Italy, United Kingdom, Spain, Canada, Japan, Poland, Argentina, Netherlands, Colombia, Ukraine, Australia, Egypt, Peru, Chile). Per task instructions, 'top relative search term per country' was preferred where published; Pornhub's 2025 report does not publish per-country relative SEARCH TERMS (only relative CATEGORIES, e.g. 'Mexico viewed the Latina category +357% more than other countries'), so top relative CATEGORY was used for all 20 countries as the documented fallback, except Spain and Japan whose per-country sections omitted a relative-category paragraph entirely (verified by close re-reading of the full text) -- for those two, Spain's top TRENDING SEARCH TERM and Japan's TOP CATEGORY were substituted respectively, each flagged in meta.kind and meta.note in the data file.

Its state list (e.g. Oregon='BDSM', Louisiana='Flogging', Connecticut='Dominate', Delaware='Sub', Washington='Spanking') does not match the Year in Review map (Oregon='horny grandma', Louisiana='thicc', Washington='pegging', etc.) because it reflects a different time window / methodology. caveats: US STATE COVERAGE GAP (structural, not a research gap): Pornhub's own 2025 Year in Review map labels only 28 states + DC (29 of 51 possible US jurisdictions). The remaining 22 states are shown gray/unlabeled on the official map because Pornhub itself has no usable data for them -- these states enacted online age-verification laws in 2024-2025 that led Pornhub to block site access rather than comply, per multiple corroborating press reports (UNILAD Tech reports 23 states blocked as of Dec 2, 2025; Them.us and other outlets report the number reached 25 by year's end per Wired). This is a limitation of the underlying Pornhub dataset itself, not an extraction failure -- there is no complete 50-state table to recover from any source for 2025. The 22 omitted states are listed explicitly above rather than fabricated or backfilled from an older year.

The 2025 map's omitted-state count (22) is slightly lower than the ~23-25 cited in press narrative text; this is expected since the map was likely finalized/captured at a specific point before additional blocks (e.g. Missouri, cited as the 23rd state blocked 'as of Dec 2, 2025') were reflected, or because a handful of blocked states still had enough residual/VPN-influenced traffic for Pornhub to include them. The map image itself (not the prose estimate) was treated as ground truth for exactly which states have entries.
DC is included as a jurisdiction (key US-DC) per task instructions ('all 50 states + DC if available') and is directly labeled on the official map with the term 'dildo sucking'.

Country-level data is TOP RELATIVE CATEGORY, not top relative SEARCH TERM, for 18 of 20 countries (all except Spain and Japan, see next caveat), because Pornhub's 2025 report does not publish a per-country relative-search-term ranking -- only a per-country relative-CATEGORY ranking (e.g., 'For top relative categories, Mexico was more likely to view the Latina category, by +357%'). This matches the task's own documented fallback ('top category if relative terms aren't published per-country'). Each country entry's meta.kind field is set to 'top_relative_category' to make this explicit and machine-checkable.

Spain and Japan are further exceptions: their per-country sections in the source text do not include a relative-category paragraph at all (verified by full re-read of both sections). Spain's entry uses its top TRENDING search term instead ('digitacion'/fingering, +778%, meta.kind = 'top_trending_search'); Japan's entry uses its overall TOP CATEGORY instead ('Japanese', meta.kind = 'top_category'). Both are flagged with distinct meta.kind values and explanatory meta.note text so they are not silently conflated with the relative-category entries for the other 18 countries.

The US country-level entry (key 'US') is included for completeness/context with the nation's #1 overall search term ('latina') but is explicitly NOT a relative measure, since the United States is the baseline every other country/state is compared against in Pornhub's relative-search methodology; its meta.kind is 'top_search_term' rather than 'top_relative_category' to avoid implying an apples-to-apples comparison with the other 19 countries.

All search terms and category names are recorded verbatim as published by Pornhub / as transcribed from the official infographic, including lowercase styling and slang/abbreviated terms (e.g. 'pawg', 'queef', 'thicc'). No terms were invented, normalized, euphemized, or censored per task instructions. Percentage figures for relative categories are copied verbatim from the source prose including the exact percentage given.
Content is explicit adult-content search/category terminology by nature of the source; this is intentional and required by the task brief, not an oversight.

One international press source (protothema.gr) reported a partially different, broader 'World's Most Viewed Categories by region' world map (e.g., grouping 'US and Australia: lesbian', 'Canada: mature women') which reflects the SAME 2025 Year in Review but a DIFFERENT, coarser regional-category map than the per-country Top-20 detail table used for this dataset's 'countries' entries -- the per-country Top-20 detail table (more granular, named-country, includes percentages) was preferred as the primary country-level source since it is more specific and is Pornhub's own headline treatment of country-level data.

A separate, unrelated Pornhub product -- a 'Valentine's Day 2025 Insights' state map republished via a retailer blog (Marquis de Mayfair) -- was found during research and explicitly excluded; see excluded_sources above. Do not conflate its state-term pairings with this Year-in-Review dataset.
